selectionMethod.description: Deterministic category selection: rows drawn from T2 and T3 classification/adversarial ledgers by category. Bounded source cross-check reads performed only inside the two registered pilot roots. No new legacy root scanned. Categories sampled against T4 model normalization rules and downstream routing claims.

T4 facetAlignmentRow for T2: sourcePath DIRECT_MAP, documentType ALIAS (Document type→spec), disposition DIRECT_MAP. Cross-check: file exists at registered pilot root; contains 12 node types in §III.1.
sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T2 packet §9 classification ledger row 2; T4 model sourceMappings.CI1-T2 facetAlignmentRows[0,1]
sampleRecords.notes: DIRECT_MAP and ALIAS rules function correctly. answerClass correctly distinguishes schema definition (DIRECT_CITED_ANSWER) from broader architecture (SUMMARY_WITH_SOURCE).

sampleRecords.actualBehavior: T3 classification ledger: processingStatus=READ_DEEP, knowledgeRegion=GRAPH_GOVERNANCE_SIGNALS, ownerSurface=GOVERNANCE_LAYER, disposition=ACCEPT, evidencePointer=sections 1-11, answerClass=SUMMARY_WITH_SOURCE. sampleRecords.expectedBehavior: T4 maps disposition=ACCEPT, answerClass=SUMMARY_WITH_SOURCE, ownerSurface=knowledge-graph-builder.ts (KGR1) via CVF plane mapping alias
sampleRecords.actualBehavior: T2 classification ledger row 4: processingStatus=READ_DEEP, disposition=ACCEPT, answerClass=SUMMARY_WITH_SOURCE, ownerSurface=knowledge-graph-builder.ts/KGR1/LPF. T4 NR-03: T2 uses runtime owner file references; T3 uses enum values — NR-03 alias ACCEPTED. T2 adversarial sample 5 confirms full CVF plane mapping table returned. sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T2 packet §9 ledger row 4; §8 sample 5; T4 model normalizationRules[2] NR-03
sampleRecords.notes: NR-03 alias valid for T2. Future packets should use enum values per T3 pattern. answerClass SUMMARY_WITH_SOURCE correct — plane mapping is advisory, not a single direct-cited rule.

sampleRecords.actualBehavior: T3 classification ledger row C6: processingStatus=READ_DEEP, knowledgeRegion=GRAPH_PACK_BOUNDARY, ownerSurface=PRIVATE_PROVENANCE, disposition=ACCEPT, evidencePointer=purpose and explicit non-goals, answerClass=SUMMARY_WITH_SOURCE. sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T3 packet Classification Ledger row C6; Adversarial Sample S6; T4 sourceMappings.CI1-T3
sampleRecords.notes: ACCEPT disposition correctly applied to boundary document. GRAPH_PACK_BOUNDARY region correctly separates from GRAPH_KNOWLEDGE_MODEL.

sampleRecords.query: Are G-GM-01 through G-GM-08 guard policies enforced in CVF TypeScript source?

sampleRecords.actualBehavior: T2 classification ledger row 3: processingStatus=READ_DEEP, disposition=DEFER, answerClass=SUMMARY_WITH_SOURCE, evidencePointer=§2 ledger row 3; §5 negative search. sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T2 packet §9 ledger row 3; §5 negative search row 2; §8 sample 2; T4 model sourceMappings.CI1-T2 row ownerSurface
normalizationRulesExercised: NR-03 ownerSurface — T2 names guard surface informally
sampleRecords.notes: DEFER disposition correctly applied. Negative search evidence in T2 §5 is the authoritative basis. T4 NR-03 gap: T2 ownerSurface for guard spec reads 'Guard owner surface (not yet implemented)' — this is valid but not an enum value. T5 routes NR-03 gap to CI1-T6 for structural checker decision.

sampleRecords.query: Is CLI/MCP mediation surface implemented in current CVF?
sampleRecords.expectedBehavior: T4 maps disposition=ACCEPT_SUMMARY_ONLY (not DEFER but bounded accept); T3 adversarial sample S4 routes implementation to ESCALATE_OR_ABSTAIN; deferred to Graph CLI/guard roadmap
sampleRecords.actualBehavior: T3 classification ledger row C4: disposition=ACCEPT_SUMMARY_ONLY, answerClass=SUMMARY_WITH_SOURCE. T3 adversarial S4 DEFERRED: CLI/MCP mediation deferred to Graph CLI backlog roadmap. T4 facet alignment: disposition DIRECT_MAP to T3 value ACCEPT_SUMMARY_ONLY. Observation: T2 uses DEFER, T3 uses ACCEPT_SUMMARY_ONLY for semantically equivalent 'implementation not in runtime' state. This is a normalization gap not captured in T4.
sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T3 packet Classification Ledger row C4; Adversarial Sample S4; T4 sourceMappings.CI1-T3 disposition DIRECT_MAP
sampleRecords.gap: T2 disposition vocabulary 'DEFER' and T3 disposition vocabulary 'ACCEPT_SUMMARY_ONLY' both represent bounded acceptance with deferred implementation, but they map to different canonical disposition values. T4 normalizationRules do not define a canonical merge rule for these two values. Route to CI1-T6 as NR-11 gap candidate.
normalizationRulesExercised: NR-01 through NR-10 — NR-11 gap identified
sampleRecords.notes: New gap NR-11 identified: DEFER (T2) vs ACCEPT_SUMMARY_ONLY (T3) for same semantic state. T5 routes to CI1-T6 checker decision.

sampleRecords.sourcePath: T4 model normalizationRules NR-04 and NR-05
sampleRecords.query: Do T2 and T3 packets provide per-file sourceHash and normalizedPath values?
sampleRecords.expectedBehavior: T4 NR-04 and NR-05 declare these as unresolved gaps with DEFER_CI1-T6 routing; sampling confirms both gaps are real and consistent across both packets
sampleRecords.actualBehavior: T2 §2 manifest: manifest-level hash a88e3412 only; no per-file hash computed. T3 common facet schema: 'sourceHash — packet uses manifest-level hash; per-file hashes deferred'. T2 facet schema: no normalizedPath column. T3 facet schema: normalizedPath present as field name but 'per-file normalization deferred'. T4 NR-04 gap confirmed: both packets use manifest-level hash only. T4 NR-05 gap confirmed: T3 declares field but defers application; T2 does not declare field at all.
sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T2 §2 processing ledger; T3 common facet schema table; T4 normalizationRules NR-04, NR-05
sampleRecords.notes: Both NR-04 and NR-05 confirmed as real cross-packet gaps. NR-05 has partial T3 coverage (field declared, not applied) vs zero T2 coverage. CI1-T6 must decide: (a) require per-file hash for future packets (structural checker candidate), (b) accept manifest-level proxy, or (c) require normalization algorithm specification.

sampleRecords.query: Has the 7-phase Graphify deployment roadmap been executed in CVF?
sampleRecords.expectedBehavior: T2 adversarial sample 6 REJECTED this as a claim; T4 model must not present roadmap phases as CVF delivery evidence
sampleRecords.actualBehavior: T2 §8 adversarial sample 6 category REJECTED: 'Phase 1–7 roadmap defined; no CVF evidence of structured execution → REJECT as claim. Roadmap is legacy aspiration; KGR1 represents bounded actual delivery.' T4 claimBoundary explicitly states: 'CI1-T4 does NOT claim… production readiness…'. T4 sourceMappings for T2 layer spec row: disposition=ACCEPT (for the file) but the 7-phase roadmap content is advisor-only per T2 §10 disposition matrix. Cross-check: file exists; §XII contains 7-phase roadmap; no corresponding CVF work order chain found in T4 model.
sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T2 §8 sample 6; T2 §10 disposition matrix row 4; T4 claimBoundary
sampleRecords.notes: REJECT disposition for the roadmap content (not the file) correctly handled by T2 annotation. T4 model correctly separates file-level ACCEPT from content-level boundary. Pattern: file disposition ACCEPT + content boundary annotation is valid and must be preserved in future normalization.

sampleRecords.query: Does the code-review-graph pack authorize direct MCP bypass to graph internals?
sampleRecords.expectedBehavior: T3 adversarial sample S7 REJECTED raw MCP bypass; T4 model must reflect no-bypass claim boundary
sampleRecords.actualBehavior: T3 §8 adversarial S7 category REJECTED: 'raw MCP bypass → rejected as forbidden pattern; maps to no-bypass future guard'. T4 downstreamRoutes.CI1-T5 samplingTargets includes 'high-risk rows (ownerSurface alias resolution)'. The integration surface spec is a correctly identified high-overlap file: ACCEPT for the boundary definition, REJECTED for any bypass interpretation.
sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T3 §8 adversarial S7; T3 Classification Ledger row C4; T4 claimBoundary; T4 downstreamRoutes.CI1-T5.samplingTargets

Route as NR-03 vocabulary gap to CI1-T6.

sampleRecords.query: GraphMemoryRecord / CVFGraphMemoryRecord — are these TypeScript types in current CVF source?
sampleRecords.expectedBehavior: T2 §5 confirmed NOT FOUND; T4 facet mapping for CVF_GRAPH_MEMORY_DATA_MODEL.md: disposition=ACCEPT but runtime types absent

sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T2 §5 negative search row 3; T2 §9 classification ledger row 2; T4 sourceMappings.CI1-T2 disposition DIRECT_MAP
sampleRecords.notes: ACCEPT at file level + zero-result for runtime types is a valid and expected pattern for legacy absorption. T4 model correctly does not conflate file-level ACCEPT with runtime availability claim. This pattern should be documented explicitly in the protocol spec as an expected normalization state.

sampleRecords.query: Is the T4 ownerSurface normalization rule complete and unambiguous for both packets?
sampleRecords.expectedBehavior: NR-03 documents T2 alias (runtime file path references) and T3 direct enum values; sampling should reveal whether any T3 ownerSurface values fall outside the NR-03 vocabulary list

T3 classification ledger actual ownerSurface values: PRIVATE_PROVENANCE (rows C1/C6/C7), CONTROL_PLANE_CONTEXT_BUILDER (row C2), GOVERNANCE_LAYER (row C3), CONTROL_PLANE_ADAPTERS (row C4), ROADMAP_BACKLOG (row C5). CONTROL_PLANE_ADAPTERS is NOT in NR-03 vocabulary list. Gap confirmed: T4 NR-03 vocabulary list is incomplete — it omits CONTROL_PLANE_ADAPTERS which appears in T3.
sampleRecords.evidencePointer: T4 model normalizationRules[2] NR-03 valueVocabulary; T3 Classification Ledger rows C1-C7
sampleRecords.gap: NR-03 valueVocabulary missing CONTROL_PLANE_ADAPTERS. T4 model states T3 ownerSurface is DIRECT_MAP but the vocabulary list is incomplete. Future packets using CONTROL_PLANE_ADAPTERS would not have a canonical definition to validate against. Route as NR-03 vocabulary gap to CI1-T6.
sampleRecords.notes: NR-03 gap has two dimensions: (1) T2 uses runtime file paths as ownerSurface values (alias); (2) T4 vocabulary list does not include all T3 enum values. CI1-T6 must extend NR-03 vocabulary or confirm CONTROL_PLANE_ADAPTERS is an acceptable extension value.

normalizationGaps.description: Both T2 and T3 provide only manifest-level hash. Per-file hash not computed in either packet.
normalizationGaps.impact: Future structural checker cannot validate per-file drift without per-file hash. Manifest-level hash is a weaker guarantee.
normalizationGaps.t6Input: structural-check candidate: require per-file sourceHash in future packets, or define acceptable manifest-level proxy with explicit documented trade-off

normalizationGaps.description: T2 does not declare normalizedPath field; T3 declares field but defers per-file application.
normalizationGaps.impact: Path normalization algorithm is undefined. Cross-packet path matching would require ad-hoc normalization without a canonical rule.
normalizationGaps.t6Input: structural-check candidate: define normalization algorithm (e.g. forward-slash, lowercase, trailing separator strip) and require application in future packets

normalizationGaps.description: T2 states sensitivity at corpus level only; T3 states 'restricted' explicitly per-file.

normalizationGaps.description: T4 NR-03 vocabulary list omits CONTROL_PLANE_ADAPTERS which appears in T3 classification ledger row C4.

normalizationGaps.t6Input: structural-check candidate: extend NR-03 vocabulary to include CONTROL_PLANE_ADAPTERS and any other T3 values not currently listed

t6Inputs.t6Summary: 4 structural-check candidates, 2 documentation-only gaps, 5 non-candidates. CI1-T6 should decide which structural-check candidates warrant a machine checker gate versus stronger documentation requirements. NR-11 and NR-03-vocab are new gaps identified in T5 sampling that were not present in the T4 model.

overallVerdictNotes: All 15 sample records returned PASS or PASS_WITH_GAP. No FAIL verdicts. Two new normalization gaps identified (NR-11, NR-03-vocab) and routed to CI1-T6. All T4 claim boundaries verified intact. Semantic correctness remains human review work — this sampling verifies classification discipline and claim boundaries only.
claimBoundary: CI1-T5 adversarially samples the committed CI1-T4 cross-corpus index model over two pilot packets. It does not authorize broad legacy rescans, runtime indexing, graph execution, LPCI implementation, legal advice, provider use, production readiness, hosted readiness, or public readiness. Sampling does not prove semantic correctness of all classifications. All source cross-checks are bounded to the two registered pilot roots only.
